extracted.intended_audience: authors/novelists preparing a synopsis for agents or submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for writing a novel synopsis intended for literary agents: what to include, what to omit, and how to present plot, characters and endings concisely. Emphasises submission-ready, one-page technical summaries that show the story arc to an agent/editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all spoilers/plot twists
rubrics_metrics.description: “Give me ALL the spoilers!” / “Do include spoilers, because the judges need to see how you will carry the narrative right through to the end.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents expect the synopsis to reveal major twists and the ending so they can judge the full story arc. Don’t try to preserve mystery in the synopsis — save suspense for the manuscript itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show major beats of the narrative (skeleton of the plot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the major beats of your narrative front of mind when writing your synopsis — include the skeleton of key events in chronological order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques: number major events (e.g., 1–10) down the page and place the first major event and the ending at endpoints, then fill in core beats; flesh these into paragraphs to create a full synopsis. Prioritise chronology and main beats over subplots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on overarching journey and main characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t get bogged down in all the subplots; focus on the overarching journey of the novel and the main characters instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover main action and character development through the piece. Treat the synopsis as the backbone of the novel rather than a blow-by-blow of every minor character or event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be succinct and concise (ideally one page)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be as succinct as possible while outlining the whole story arc; preference for one page synopses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit detail, avoid extraneous anecdotes (e.g., secondary narrative detours). If constrained to one page, omit lesser subplots and prioritise the crucial events and characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include who/when/where/catalyst/resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the who, when, where, catalyst and resolution — the synopsis is the who, what, where and when of your novel, and should show how it ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear the protagonist(s), setting and inciting incident, then describe how the central conflict resolves. Explicitly state the ending rather than leaving it implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat synopsis as a technical document, not a sales pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: A synopsis is a technical document that no reader will ever see — it’s just for the agent and publisher. It is not on its own going to sell your book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on clarity and completeness of plot information rather than trying to beautify the prose. Agents will judge manuscript quality separately; the synopsis’s role is informational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude motivations/backstory/details that belong in the manuscript ('not the why')
rubrics_metrics.description: The synopsis is not the 'why' — motivation, detail and backstory belong in the novel itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep internal motivations and extended backstory minimal unless essential to understanding plot beats. Emphasise events and outcomes over internal exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise key information: main characters, setting, plot, resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Needs all the key information: main characters, setting, plot, resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure these elements are clearly present in the synopsis. If space is tight, cut subplots rather than omitting these essentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit named characters to avoid confusion
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s wise to limit yourself to 4 or 5 character names if possible, to avoid confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name only characters essential to the main arc; refer to minor players by role (e.g., 'the detective', 'her sister') rather than full names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show the story’s uniqueness / selling points
rubrics_metrics.description: Always think about what makes your book unique. Is it the setting? The circumstances? The concept? The narrator?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure the synopsis communicates the book’s distinctive hook(s) so the agent can see why it stands out, but do so succinctly within the plot summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid chapter/character breakdowns and stilted formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t include character or chapter breakdowns as that just makes for a very stilted read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write flowing paragraphs that summarise the narrative rather than a list of chapters or rigid bullet-point character breakdowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity above ornate prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity is what I look for in a synopsis: condensing your story into one page shows understanding of your narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, well-structured synopsis demonstrates narrative control. Good sentence-level writing helps, but clarity and comprehension are primary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopses and extracts should work in sympatico
rubrics_metrics.description: The extract and synopsis are equally important and should be working in sympatico completely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the synopsis aligns with any sample pages/extracts you submit — they should tell a consistent story about tone, main events and characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use visual or oral techniques to test and refine the synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Visualising often helps — try plotting a map or chart of key action/emotional beats; or say the story out loud to someone to test clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parts of the synopsis make listeners’ eyes glaze or fail to engage, those parts need pruning or reframing. Use external readers to spot unclear sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get feedback from readers who have read the book
rubrics_metrics.description: Show it to a few people who have read your book, ask if there is anything they’d change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use trusted readers to confirm the synopsis captures the book’s arc, pacing and key reveals. Feedback helps identify missing beats or confusing summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: It’s acceptable if the synopsis isn’t perfectly literary
rubrics_metrics.description: If the novel is fantastic, I don’t care in the slightest if you can’t write the perfect synopsis... it doesn’t have to be beautifully written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents will prioritise manuscript quality; a basic, clear synopsis is fine. Don’t let perfectionism about the synopsis stop you from submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refine the synopsis at different manuscript stages
rubrics_metrics.description: It can be helpful to try writing a synopsis at different stages of the manuscript — especially if you are stuck.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafting synopses during development can reveal structural weaknesses and help tighten the narrative before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: A synopsis should read like a short, simple map of the book
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on your novel and make the synopsis a short, simple map of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for an overview that lets an agent quickly understand the route of the story from inciting incident to resolution, rather than exhaustive detail.
